rationale: Honey-bee workers do destroy surplus queen cells when the colony is not swarming, and they ball failing or surplus queens so that one queen remains. Queens also kill rival queens themselves, so it is not accurate that workers kill most queens as a routine.

Honey bees show strong flower constancy within a foraging trip, but they do switch plant species before returning, especially when rewards change. The absolute claim that a bee never visits another kind until it is back at the hive does not hold.
Human multiple births above five are well documented, including sextuplets and higher-order sets, both with and without fertility treatment. Five is not the maximum.

Honey-bee age polyethism runs the other way: young workers nurse and build inside the hive, and older workers forage outside. Foragers wear smooth and lose hair, whereas younger bees are the fuzzier ones.
Most bony fishes have bony opercula, and sharks and rays have open gill slits. Cartilage does not by itself explain the missing cover: other cartilaginous fishes, the chimaeras, have an operculum.

Paired horns and antlers occur in cloven-hoofed ruminants, and no solid-hoofed equid has a pair of horns. Rhinoceros horns are midline keratin structures on a three-toed foot, so they do not break the paired-horn clause.

Dolphins are placental and viviparous, with two inguinal mammary glands opening as slits beside the genital slit rather than as chest teats. Milk is ejected from those slits, and the nipples are not ordinarily visible.
In insects that copulate, the male almost always inserts an intromittent organ into the female. Female-into-male coupling is a rare exception, not the rule for flies, beetles, or insects generally.
Hair and hair-derived spines mark mammals, and nearly all mammals bear live young. Platypuses and echidnas are hairy or spiny and lay eggs, so the universal claim fails.
Elephant pregnancy lasts about 18 to 22 months, close to two years, and a single calf is the normal birth. Twins occur but are very rare, so the uniparous claim is nearly right.

In Aristotle's catfish the male stays on the nest, fans the eggs, and drives off small fish while the female leaves. Guarding lasts for weeks, though a fixed span of forty to fifty days is only an approximation.
European eels are born from eggs spawned in the Sargasso Sea, and the larvae migrate to European rivers. They do not arise spontaneously from worms in mud.
The loud cicada song is produced by male tymbals; females lack that organ and are silent in the ordinary sense. Females of some species make soft wing clicks, which is not the calling song.
Rabies is a fatal viral disease of dogs and of other mammals bitten by them. Untreated humans also develop rabies and die, so the exception for man is false.
Hair follicles stop producing hair at death. The appearance of longer hair is skin shrinkage and dehydration, not continued growth.
Humans, sheep, goats, and pigs have the same dental formula in both sexes. Males do not systematically have a higher tooth count.

Many animal hybrids besides mules are sterile or have sharply reduced fertility, including a number of mammal and bird crosses. Mules are usually sterile, but rare fertile female mules show that even they are not invariably so.
Semen carries germline gametes, not material drawn from every organ of the parent. Inheritance of that pangenetic sort is rejected by modern genetics.

Partridges, quails, and many other ground-nesting birds perform injury-feigning distraction displays that lead a predator away from chicks. The broken-wing or lameness act, followed by return to the brood, is well established.

Most eggs of broadcast-spawning fishes die before hatching, and high fecundity compensates for that mortality in evolutionary terms. Many oviparous fishes instead guard fewer eggs, so the pattern is a strong tendency rather than a rule for every fish.
Octopuses have eight arms, but squid and cuttlefish have eight arms plus two long tentacles, and nautiluses have many more tentacles. The claim that every cephalopod has eight feet is false.

Pregnant brown bears give birth in the winter den, do not eat while denned, and bring cubs out in spring, often around a few months after the winter solstice. Denning length varies with climate, but the seasonal pattern is right.
Many scaly bony fishes bear live young, and many sharks, skates, and rays lay eggs. The anglerfish is a bony fish, not the sole egg-laying exception among cartilaginous fishes.

European eels are oviparous and spawn after a paired migration to the Sargasso Sea. River-caught eels are immature, which is why milt and eggs are not seen inland, but the reproductive organs exist and mature at sea.
Some sharks, including smooth-hounds, form a yolk-sac placenta so the embryo continues development attached to the uterine wall after the yolk is used. The egg is retained for the whole gestation.
Humans do grey with age, and horses can grey, but greying of the muzzle and face is also obvious in dogs and in other mammals. It is not practically confined to humans and horses.
The female argonaut's thin shell is an egg case, and she swims rather than sailing. The story that she spreads a web as a sail and uses her arms as oars is not supported by observation.

Spider-hunting wasps and mud-daubers stock mud cells or burrows with spiders and seal them, and the larva consumes the provision. They typically paralyze the spider rather than kill it outright, and true ichneumon wasps usually parasitize hosts in place.
The human thorax normally has twelve pairs of ribs, occasionally eleven or thirteen. Eight pairs is not the human count.
Partridge eggs are fertilized by copulation. A hen is not impregnated by standing downwind of a male, by hearing him, or by his breath.
In many quadrupeds the right kidney sits farther forward than the left, but in humans the right kidney is usually the lower one because of the liver. The claim does not hold for all animals.

The honey-bee queen lays the fertilized eggs that become both workers and new queens, with caste set by cell and diet. She is the source of both kinds, though drones come from unfertilized eggs as well.
Swans vocalize through life, and there is no special death song or flight out to sea to die. The swan-song story is legendary.
The elephant trunk is an elongated nose, and elephants swimming or wading in deep water raise it above the surface and breathe through it. That use as a snorkel is routine.

Humans have a very high encephalization quotient among large animals, but several small mammals and birds have higher brain-to-body mass ratios. Brains are not ranked by moistness, and the human brain is not the moistest.

In temperate yellowjackets and paper wasps the workers and males die as winter comes, and only mated queens overwinter to found the next colony. Some populations in mild climates keep perennial colonies, so the rule is not quite universal.
Female octopuses guard their egg strings and typically stop feeding, lose condition, and die about when the eggs hatch. Brooding anorexia is standard in octopus.

A honey-bee worker's barbed sting lodges in elastic skin and tears out the sting apparatus, after which the bee dies. The lost tissue is the sting and its glands more than the whole intestine, and stings delivered to other insects need not be fatal.
The crocodile's lower jaw hinges and moves, as in other jawed vertebrates. The upper jaw only seems to rise because the animal lifts its head.
Crabs, crayfish, and lobsters moult repeatedly through life, and the new cuticle is soft until it hardens. Ecdysis is not a single event.

Grey mullets move from the sea into estuaries, marshes, and rivers to feed, and adult European eels leave fresh water and migrate to the sea to spawn. Young eels also ascend rivers, so the eel movement is not only downstream.
Scorpion young ride on the mother and do not kill her after birth. Matriphagy occurs in a few spiders, not in spiders generally, and not as a rule for scorpions.

Many temperate snakes and lizards brumate and fast in winter, but the duration is not a fixed four months and tropical species stay active. The Nile crocodile does not spend four winter months hidden without feeding.

Oysters, cockles, limpets, barnacles, and sea squirts come from eggs and larvae, often with planktonic stages, not from spontaneous generation in mud. Substrate preferences are real, but the origin claimed for them is not.
Lice infest many birds and mammals, but not every individual, and donkeys do get both lice and ticks. The claimed exception is false.
The brain is densely supplied with arteries, veins, and capillaries and runs near body temperature. It is neither bloodless nor naturally cold.

Most hawks, eagles, and falcons are territorial rather than flocking. Vultures roost and feed socially, and several raptors nest colonially or hunt in groups, so the universal ban on gregariousness fails.
Swallows, storks, turtle-doves, and kites migrate rather than hibernating featherless in holes. A few birds use torpor, but not the species named here.

Combers and related serranids are simultaneous hermaphrodites, so specimens carry ovarian tissue and pure males are not found. They are not literally packed with ripe eggs at every season, so the wording is stronger than the biology.

The common cuckoo is not a hawk and not a transformed hawk: it lacks raptorial talons and is itself taken by hawks. Hawks do sometimes kill other birds of prey, so the claim that this never happens within one kind is too absolute.

Many light-eyed babies are born with blue-grey irises that later darken, but many children, especially in darker-skinned populations, are born with brown eyes that stay brown. Other mammals, including kittens, also show early blue eyes.
Horned or antlered ruminants lack upper incisors, have a four-chambered stomach, and chew the cud. That joint pattern holds for cattle, sheep, goats, and deer.
Children tend to resemble parents and earlier kin, and recessive or polygenic traits can skip a generation and reappear in grandchildren. That is ordinary Mendelian and quantitative inheritance.
Sensation is processed in the brain, not in the heart. Brain tissue lacks some pain receptors, but that does not make the brain incapable of causing sensation.
The arm a male octopus inserts into the female is the hectocotylus, a modified arm that transfers spermatophores. It is a copulatory organ, not merely a holdfast outside the reproductive system.

Humans outlive elephants, whose typical lifespan is shorter than a human one. Tortoises, bowhead whales, and some sharks and clams live longer than humans, so neither the ranking nor the elephant exception holds.
Pigeons and doves are socially monogamous and often keep the same mate for years, sometimes until one dies. Pairs also divorce, and extra-pair matings occur, which the statement partly allows.

Living mammals do not combine true horns with tusks, and carnivores with shearing teeth have neither. A few extinct hoofed mammals carried both large canines and horn-like skull structures, so the absolute version is not airtight.
The common kingfisher in Europe nests in spring and summer, not around the winter solstice. The midwinter breeding story belongs to legend rather than to the bird's season.
Bivalves, snails, barnacles, and sea squirts reproduce sexually, whether the sexes are separate or combined in hermaphrodites. Sessile animals are not sexless, and many plants are dioecious as well.
Electric rays have paired electric organs and discharge them to stun prey. The shock is strong enough to numb a person who handles one.
Fishes suffer contagious epidemics, including viral hemorrhagic disease, herpesvirus outbreaks, and bacterial kills that sweep through populations. Individual illness is real, and so are pestilences.

The fig wasp develops in caprifigs, enters the edible fig, and pollinates it so that fruit of the Smyrna type sets and stays on the tree. Hanging wild figs in orchards is the traditional practice of caprification.
Destroying a cock's testes produces a capon whose comb pales, who stops crowing, and who loses sexual behavior. Birds castrated before those traits develop do not acquire them.

The story of a small bird cleaning a crocodile's teeth in safety is a long-standing anecdote, usually attached to the Egyptian plover. Reliable field evidence that this is regular mutualism is lacking.

The common cuckoo builds no nest and lays, usually one egg, in a smaller host's nest, and the host rears the chick. The female typically removes one host egg, while the nestling ejects the rest, so the adult does not devour the whole clutch.
Male sharks, dogfish, and other elasmobranchs have a pair of claspers beside the cloaca, and females do not. The sex difference is general across these fishes.

At night open water is often warmer than the air because water cools more slowly, and Nile crocodiles spend much time in the water. They also come ashore at night, so the habit is not a strict rule explained only by that temperature difference.
Bees secrete wax from abdominal glands; they do not collect it as a product of flowers. Honey is nectar or honeydew that workers gather and ripen, not dew deposited from the air.

Castration before puberty prevents the voice from breaking and prevents growth of the androgen-dependent beard and body hair. Male-pattern baldness also depends on androgens, so men castrated in boyhood do not go bald in that pattern.
Embryonic organs differentiate in sequence from germ layers; they are not all present in miniature from the start. That epigenetic course is directly visible in developing embryos.
Many animals that move about are hermaphrodites, including earthworms, land snails, and some fishes. Many plants have separate sexes, so neither half of the contrast holds as a universal.

The smooth-hound nourishes late embryos through a yolk-sac placenta attached to the uterine wall, with extraembryonic membranes, after the yolk is used up. The parallel with mammalian pregnancy is anatomically real.
Fishes hear with inner ears and otoliths and smell with paired olfactory organs opening in the nares. They are not limited to eyes.

Some congenital blindness and limb defects are heritable, but lameness, scars, and pimples acquired in life are not passed to children. The general claim that deformities and marks are inherited is false.
In most insect species that mate, females are larger than males, a pattern tied to fecundity. Male-larger species exist but are the minority.
Bird sex is fixed at fertilization by sex chromosomes, not by whether the egg is pointed or round. Egg shape does not determine whether a chick is female or male.

Crab claws are often asymmetric, but the larger claw is not invariably the right one, and spiny lobsters lack such crushing claws. In the clawed lobster, which side carries the crusher is roughly a matter of chance, and that part alone is right.

Domestic dogs usually whelp about 63 days after ovulation, and 60 to 63 days is a fair central range counted in the traditional way. Litters a little earlier than 60 days from mating can survive, so the hard lower bound is too strict.

Hyenas are not hermaphrodites; each animal is male or female with one set of gonads. Female spotted hyenas have a masculinized clitoris that causes the confusion, whereas the claim that both sexes merely share a female-like mark under the tail is only a rough description.
Human semen is whitish or greyish in every population. It is not black in dark-skinned people.
Head-first delivery is the normal presentation in humans and in most hoofed mammals. Whales and dolphins are normally born tail first, so birth is not head first in all viviparous animals.
Dolphins, porpoises, and whales are all placental mammals and give birth to live young. None of them carries or lays eggs.
Octopuses match nearby stones and other substrates by changing skin color and texture, both while hunting and when disturbed. Chromatophore camouflage of this kind is routine.
The lion has the usual mammalian series of cervical vertebrae, seven separate bones. Its neck is not a single bone.
Many large birds delay breeding, but most bird species are small songbirds that breed in their first year. It is not true that very few birds do so.

A breeding pair of eagles uses a large territory and drives off other eagles and competing raptors, and fledged young eventually disperse. Many smaller birds nest near eagle nests, so eagles do not keep other birds from settling nearby.

In the hen's egg the embryonic heart appears early as a small red pulsating mass, and paired vitelline vessels run from the circulation it establishes. The visible beating speck is a real stage of development.

Common cranes breed across northern Eurasia, including the steppe, and many winter in the Nile valley, Sudan, and Ethiopia. They do not all fly to the marshes at the river's ultimate source, and many stop farther north.
Honey bees do not pick up stones to steady themselves in wind. The ballast story has no basis in their flight behavior.

Female-larger size is the common pattern in sharks, rays, and many other fishes, consistent with selection for fecundity. A substantial minority of species has larger males, so the claim holds as a majority tendency.
Boys usually begin producing semen around fourteen, at spermarche. They are capable of fathering children well before twenty-one, so the second age is not the onset of fertility.
Hens and geese that have never mated lay unfertilized eggs. Those wind-eggs are not leftovers of an earlier impregnation.
Acquired mutilations such as amputations and scars are not transmitted to offspring, who therefore are not always mutilated when a parent is. Offspring also routinely differ from their parents.
Dogs, lions, wolves, foxes, and jackals are born with sealed eyelids that open days later. Not every many-toed quadruped is altricial in that way: spotted hyena cubs are born with their eyes open.

Butterfly caterpillars, and the larvae of bees and wasps, feed and pass waste, while the pupa does not feed. A pupa may void a meconium at the end of metamorphosis, but it does not feed or excrete through the pupal stage.
Men and women have the same cranial sutures: coronal, sagittal, and lambdoid. Women do not have a single circular suture where men have three.

Across animals, larger body size tends to go with fewer offspring and smaller size with more, as in elephants versus mice. Important exceptions include tiny bats with single young and huge fishes that shed vast numbers of eggs.

The anglerfish fishes with a slender illicium and a fleshy lure on the head, often while partly buried, and strikes at fish that approach the bait. The filament-lure account matches the anatomy and the hunting behavior.
Many sharks, rays, and bony fishes give birth to live young and breathe water with gills. Internal viviparity does not require air breathing.
In vertebrates the heart is among the first organs to become distinct and functional, and it is the center of the early circulation. It is not the origin from which the other body parts are formed.

Humans laugh, but great apes show play faces and pant-like play vocalizations when tickled, and rats emit tickle-induced ultrasonic calls and seek the stimulation. Neither laughter-like play nor ticklishness is confined to humans.
